claim: AgentRuntimeConfig in src/sqllens/config.py must reject an unknown key under [agent] (e.g. a misspelt `standing_instruction`) at load, so the key is not silently dropped and `sqllens validate` does not report success.

prior_evidence: The finding still holds at head. AgentRuntimeConfig (src/sqllens/config.py:433-492) has no model_config; it is a plain BaseModel, so unknown keys are ignored. Sibling sections ProfilesConfig (247), ResultMaskingConfig (267) and AuditConfig (419) set extra="forbid". The comment at config.py:417 says the top-level Config(extra="forbid") does not propagate into nested models and that a silent revert from a typo'd key is the worst outcome. So a misspelt [agent] standing_instruction key is dropped at load, the new rule (standing_instructions, line 465, added by this PR) never reaches the prompt, and validation passes. I searched config.py and src/sqllens for extra/forbid and found no other unknown-key check. No defect does not apply, because the failing reader is the operator, who loses a deployment rule silently. No disputed, rejection or criteria exemption was applied.

Tests (test_system_prompt.py:495-499 helper, 520-548) assert only the inner BEGIN/instructions/END block and phrases via `in section`; lines 609 and 626 pin only the prefix with the header. No test pins header/preamble/BEGIN separation. I searched the head view for authored text promising the separators and found none (no criteria_file supplied, so the No defect reason is unavailable). The section builder's own returned elements show blank separators were intended. Impact is cosmetic prompt layout.
